The nodes of the stationary wave occur on the string at P, Q, R and S. Point X is moving down at
time t = 0. The points on the string vibrate with time period T and maximum amplitude 2 cm.
The displacement s is positive in the upward direction.
Which graph best shows the variation with t of the displacement s of point Y on the string?

hints: Notice the string is straight at $t = 0$, so both X and Y start at $s = 0$, and X is given as moving down.
Remember adjacent loops PQ, QR and RS in a stationary wave vibrate in antiphase, so use X in loop PQ to work out the starting direction of loop RS containing Y.
Check where Y sits between node R and S compared to the centre of the loop, so its maximum $|s|$ must be less than the $2\text{ cm}$ antinode value.
walkthrough: At $t = 0$ the diagram shows the string flat along PS, so displacement $s = 0$ for every point, including Y. The motion is therefore starting from equilibrium, not from a peak.
Point X is in loop PQ and is moving down, so just after $t = 0$ loop PQ goes to negative $s$. In a stationary wave neighbouring loops are in antiphase.
Loop QR must therefore move opposite to PQ, upward to positive $s$, and loop RS must move opposite to QR, downward to negative $s$. So Y must leave $s = 0$ toward negative values.

Y is marked between R and S but not at the centre of loop RS where amplitude is maximum $2\text{ cm}$. A point nearer a node has smaller simple harmonic amplitude, so the $s$-$t$ curve for Y must peak at $|s| < 2\text{ cm}$.

Over half a period $T/2$ the point goes from $0$ to maximum displacement and back to $0$. A negative-going start with reduced amplitude matches the curve that dips to about $-1\text{ cm}$ and returns to zero at $T/2$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Starts at $s = 0$ moving negative and has amplitude less than $2\text{ cm}$ because Y is off the antinode and in antiphase to X's neighbour loop.

B.explanation: Starts negative but reaches $-2\text{ cm}$, which is the antinode amplitude, while Y is between node R and antinode so its amplitude is smaller.

C.explanation: Has reduced amplitude but starts positive, which would mean Y initially moves up, opposite to the antiphase requirement from X moving down.

D.explanation: Starts positive with full $2\text{ cm}$ amplitude, which is wrong for both initial direction and for Y's position away from the antinode.
